newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices mostly steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices mostly steady.

text.p: U.S. bulk millfeed prices were mostly steady on Monday amid featureless activity, dealers said.

"The only thing that is bullish is that the flour mills are not running very well this week," a dealer said, referring to the approaching Easter holiday. "But I personally think that has already been factored into the market," he added.
Also, livestock producers have begun to put animals out on pastures and cut back on supplemental feeding in parts of Oklahoma, Kansas and Texas, an annual scenario that reduces demand for middlings.
"It's springtime in Texas and Oklahoma and livestock are on the grass. It's that simple," another dealer said.
A dealer who does business in North and South Carolina also noted the bearish tone in prices at least for this week, in line with lower CBOT corn values.
He added less expensive substitutes such as soy hull and hominy continued to work their way into the market.
"Springtime is here and demand has really fallen off. There there is not much activity going on," a Kansas dealer said.
